absent: Numeric values of the scan-outcome enumeration, collapse event counters and threshold ceilings.
Second half of file collapse after small-folio accumulation, including data copy, index-tree replacement and rollback details.
Allocation, charging and node-selection policy for new huge folios beyond occupancy counting.
Full behavior of the multi-size collapse installer invoked after a successful scan.
Upper page-table allocation helpers, fault-path PMD installer and folio reference primitives owned by other dossiers.
Background scheduler state, slot insertion, progress accounting across PMDs and configuration controls.
Exact translation-flush, reverse-map and grace-period mechanisms used around table mutation.

findings.text: Provides deferred reclamation of a page table page after its PMD entry has been collapsed. The caller supplies the owning address space and the table to retire, and the callee schedules asynchronous release so that concurrent readers protected by grace periods can finish first.

Public wrapper that attempts to replace small mappings of an already huge cached folio with one PMD mapping at the containing aligned address. It forwards the address space, address and install choice to the internal file helper and discards the detailed scan outcome.

Installs a PMD mapping for a folio at an address inside a VMA. When no PMD pointer is given it walks and creates the upper table levels, then delegates to the fault-path installer and holds an extra folio reference on success. The address-space lock for the VMA must already be held.

File path used when the cache already holds a huge folio but the process still uses small entries. It checks that a file VMA fully covers the aligned extent, locks the folio from the mapping, verifies each present entry targets the expected subpage, clears entries under notification and lock protection, retires the empty table and optionally installs the PMD.

Reclaims empty page tables that block huge mapping of a file offset. It iterates reverse mappings of the offset under the inverse-map read lock, skips unsuitable VMAs or PMD states, notifies range observers, collapses the PMD entry while holding table locks, then accounts the removal and defers freeing of the old table.

Prepares collapse of one aligned file range. It allocates and initializes a new locked huge folio associated with the target mapping and start index, ensures index-tree capacity for the whole span, then walks constituent indices acquiring and validating each small folio, isolating it, unmapping it and accumulating it for a later copy phase not shown here.

Anonymous collapse scan enforces ceilings on empty, swapped and shared slots. Exceeding the empty-entry ceiling, the swap-entry ceiling or the shared-folio ceiling aborts the scan with a distinct outcome and event accounting. The empty-entry ceiling is relaxed only when the PMD order alone is enabled.

Candidate small pages must resolve to ordinary anonymous folios that are not device memory, live on the reclaim list, are unlocked, show no unexpected extra references, avoid lazy-free state unless policy allows, belong to an acceptable node and contribute to per-node occupancy tallies used for later allocation preference.

Background collapse requires evidence of use. With no referenced slots, or with swapped slots present but referenced slots below half of the PMD span, the scan reports lack of references rather than success. Other contexts bypass this use check.

Write-protection for userfault blocks collapse on every path. Armed protection on present entries or on swap entries aborts the anonymous scan, protected VMAs are rejected for huge-install collapse and are never treated as eligible for table recycling.

A file VMA qualifies for table retraction only when it has no private anonymous state, carries no userfault or related per-entry protection and shows no guard-region marker. The guard check is ordered against the table lock so it stays valid even when no address-space or VMA lock is held.

PTE-mapped huge collapse checks entry identity twice. An early walk requires every non-empty entry to be present and to reference the matching subpage of the locked huge folio. After notification and relocking, a second walk revalidates presence and identity before batched clearing, reverse-map adjustment and counter updates.

File collapse treats shmem and other files differently. Missing shmem slots count as holes that may need charging, stale shmem entries are fetched without allocation, while missing entries elsewhere trigger readahead and locked fetch. Dirty or writeback state aborts collapse for non-shmem files, with a one-time flush only when the file is not open for write.

Before joining the collapse list each small folio must be locked, current, of small order, still attached to the target mapping, isolated from reclaim, freed of private buffers and unmapped from user tables, showing only the expected references for cache membership plus isolation plus the local pin. Failures return the folio to reclaim and abort.

Anonymous scan holds the address-space read lock while mapping the table under its spinlock and advancing progress per slot. On success both are released before invoking the actual collapse routine, and a flag records that the address-space lock was dropped across that call.

Table mutation paths nest locks from address-space lock outermost through inverse-map read lock and folio lock to PMD lock outermost and table spinlock innermost, with nested acquisition when the two table locks differ. Range notification brackets the mutation. Private VMAs with armed userfault take the PMD lock earlier to exclude atomic insertion races.

File preparation guards index-tree mutation with the tree lock held with interrupts disabled, dropping it around blocking folio acquisition or reclaim work and revalidating the loaded entry after relocking. Each small folio stays locked across tree-lock release to exclude truncation, and unmapping uses batched requests with a final synchronization before copying.

Slot collection for a finished address space requires the global slot lock held. When the address space has exited, the slot is unlinked from its list, returned to its cache and its address-space reference is dropped.

Collapse control aggregates scan progress, a presence bitmap over PMD slots, per-node occupancy counts, a background-context indicator and address-range state for the current attempt. The occupancy counts steer later huge-page allocation toward the most represented node, and the bitmap records which slots were occupied.

PMD installation uses a fault descriptor carrying the target VMA, address and PMD location with cleared flags. Table-clear paths use a range-notification descriptor carrying the address space with aligned start and end and a clear-type operation to bracket invalidation around mutation.

Collapse helpers communicate through a shared scan-outcome enumeration. Success leads to PMD installation or continued accumulation, while distinct outcomes report missing tables, already huge state, VMA mismatch, protection or guard blocks, unsuitable folio state, locking or reference failures, truncation, dirtiness and external abort, each with matching unwind of locks, notifications and references.

Several validations are racy by design and depend on later rechecks. External pin counts can change between scan and install, entries can be replaced by copy, swap or migration across the notification window, and privileged operations can insert entries without the address-space lock, so mutation paths revalidate entry identity and PMD sameness under table locks before clearing.

Clearing entries before PMD install must update reverse maps and counters, defer translation flushing until the PMD flush step, decrement the table count, run table checking and defer table freeing. Abort paths that already cleared entries must still flush translations to avoid stale mappings.

PMD huge-page geometry is described by HPAGE_PMD_ORDER, HPAGE_PMD_NR, HPAGE_PMD_SIZE, HPAGE_PMD_MASK, PAGE_SIZE and PAGE_SHIFT. Collapse aligns a start down with the mask, spans one full PMD size, iterates one slot per constituent base page and converts file offsets with the base shift.

Collapse policy uses VM_DROPPABLE, VM_SHARED, TVA_FORCED_COLLAPSE, PMD_ORDER and VMA_MAYBE_GUARD_BIT. Additional gating state includes address-space exit, swap-backed marking for new shmem folios and uptodate, dirty, writeback, locked, LRU and anon folio indicators.
